questions.q: $\int_0^1 x \sin \pi x d x$ is equal to
questions.solution: $\begin{array}{rl}\int_0^1 & x \sin \pi x d x \\ \quad & =\left[-x \frac{\cos \pi x}{\pi}\right]_0^1+\int_0^1 \frac{\cos \pi x}{\pi} d x \\ \quad=\left[-x \frac{\cos \pi x}{\pi}+\frac{\sin \pi x}{\pi^2}\right]_0^1=\left[\frac{-(-1)}{\pi}\right]=\frac{1}{\pi}\end{array}$

questions.q: The value of $\int_0^{\sqrt{\ln (\pi / 2)}} \cos \left(e^{x^2}\right) 2 x e^{x^2} d x$ is
questions.solution:
Given, $I=\int_0^{\sqrt{\ln (\pi / 2)}} \cos \left(e^{x^2}\right) \cdot 2 x e^{x^2} d x$
Put $\quad e^{x^2}=t \Rightarrow 2 x e^{x^2} d x=d t$
Now, lower limit, $t=1$
Upper limit, $t=e^{\ln \pi / 2}=\frac{\pi}{2}\therefore \quad I=\int_1^{\pi / 2} \cos (t) d t=[\sin t]_1^{\pi / 2}=\sin \left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)-\sin 1\Rightarrow \quad I=1-\sin 1$

questions.q: By Simpson's $\frac{1}{3}$ rd rule, the approximate value of the integral $\int_1^2 e^{-x / 2} d x$ using four intervals, is
questions.solution:
Given integral is $\int_1^2 e^{-x / 2} d x$
On dividing interval $[1,2]$ in four parts, we have
$h=\frac{2-1}{4}=\frac{1}{4}$
Now, value of $f(x)=e^{-x / 2}$ is given below
$\begin{array}{c|c|c|c|c|c}\hline x & 1 & \frac{5}{4} & \frac{3}{2} & \frac{7}{4} & e \\\hline f(x) & 0.6065 & 0.5352 & 0.4724 & 0.4168 & 0.3679 \\\hline\end{array}
Now, Simpson's $\frac{1}{3}$ rule is
$\begin{aligned} \int_{x_0}^{x_0+n h} f(x) d x= & \frac{h}{3} \\ & {\left[\left(y_0+y_n\right)+4\left(y_1+y_3+\ldots+y_{n-1}\right)\right.} \\ & \left.+2\left(y_2+y_4+\ldots+y_{n-2}\right)\right]\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} \therefore \int_1^2 e^{-x / 2} d x= & \frac{1}{12}[(0.6065+0.3679) \\ & +4(0.5352+0.4168)+2(0.4724)]\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & =\frac{1}{12}[0.9744+3.808+0.9448] \\ & =\frac{1}{12} \times 5.7272=0.477\end{aligned}

questions.q: $\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}} \frac{\sin ^n \theta}{\sin ^n \theta+\cos ^n \theta} d \theta$ is equal to
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \text { Let } I=\int_0^{\pi / 2} \frac{\sin ^n \theta}{\sin ^n \theta+\cos ^n \theta} d \theta....(i) \\ & =\int_0^{\pi / 2} \frac{\sin ^n(\pi / 2-\theta)}{\sin ^n(\pi / 2-\theta)+\cos ^n(\pi / 2-\theta)} d \theta \\ & =\int_0^{\pi / 2} \frac{\cos ^n \theta}{\cos ^n \theta+\sin ^n \theta} d \theta....(ii) \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The value of $\int_{\sqrt{\ln 2}}^{\sqrt{\ln 3}} \frac{x \sin x^2}{\sin x^2+\sin \left(\ln 6-x^2\right)} d x$ is
questions.solution:
Let $\quad I=\int_{\sqrt{\ln 2}}^{\sqrt{\ln 3}} \frac{x \sin x^2}{\sin x^2+\sin \left(\ln 6-x^2\right)} d x$
Putting $x^2=t\Rightarrow \quad 2 x d x=d t\therefore \quad I=\frac{1}{2} \int_{\ln 2}^{\ln 3} \frac{\sin t}{\sin t+\sin (\ln 6-t)} d t$  ...(i)
Using $\int_a^b f(x) d x=\int_a^b f(a+b-x) d x$, we get
$I=\frac{1}{2} \int_{\ln 2}^{\ln 3} \frac{\sin (\ln 6-t)}{\sin (\ln 6-t)+\sin t} d t$  ...(ii)
On adding Eqs.(i) and (ii), we get
$2 I=\int_{\ln 2}^{\ln 3} 1 d t=[t]_{\ln 2}^{\ln 3}\begin{array}{ll}\Rightarrow \quad & 2 I=\frac{1}{2}(\ln 3-\ln 2)=\frac{1}{2} \ln \left(\frac{3}{2}\right) \\ \Rightarrow \quad & I=\frac{1}{4} \ln \left(\frac{3}{2}\right)\end{array}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $\int_0^{2 a} \frac{f(x)}{f(x)+f(2 a-x)} d x$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Let $I=\int_0^{2 a} \frac{f(x)}{f(x)+f(2 a-x)} d x...(i)I=\int_0^{2 a} \frac{f(2 a-x)}{f(2 a-x)+f(x)} d x...(ii)$
On adding Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get
$\begin{aligned}
2 I & =\int_0^{2 a} \frac{f(2 a-x)+f(x)}{f(2 a-x)+f(x)} d x=\int_0^{2 a} d x=2 a \\
\Rightarrow I & =a
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The value of $\int_{1 / n}^{(a n-1) / n} \frac{\sqrt{x}}{\sqrt{a-x}+\sqrt{x}} d x$ is equal to

questions.solution:
The given limit
$\begin{aligned} & L=\lim _{n \rightarrow \infty}\left\{\frac{1}{n a}+\frac{1}{n a+1}+\frac{1}{n a+2}+\ldots+\right. \\ &\left.\qquad \frac{1}{n a+n(b-a)}\right\}\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & =\lim _{n \rightarrow \infty} \sum_{r=0}^{n(b-a)} \frac{1}{n a+r} \\ & =\lim _{n \rightarrow \infty} \frac{1^{(b-a) n}}{\sum_{r=0}^{(b-a} \frac{1}{a+r / n}} \\ & =\int_0^{(b-a)} \frac{d x}{a+x}=[\log (a+x)]_0^{b-a} \quad\left(\frac{r}{n}=x\right) \\ & =\log b-\log a \\ & =\log \left(\frac{b}{a}\right)\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The value of $\int_a^b \frac{|x|}{x} d x$ is
questions.solution:
Case I. If $0 \leq a \lt b$, then $\frac{|x|}{x}=1\therefore \quad I=\int_a^b 1 \cdot d x=b-a=|b|-|a|$
Case II: If $a \lt b \leq 0$, then $|x|=-x\therefore \quad I=\int_a^b \frac{-x}{x} d x=\int_a^b(-1) d x=[-x]_a^b=-b-(-a)=|b|-|a|$
Case III If $a \lt 0 \lt b$.
then $|x|=-x \quad$ when $a \lt x \lt 0$
and $|x|=x \quad$ when $0 \lt x \lt bI=\int_a^b \frac{|x|}{x} d x \quad=\int_a^0 \frac{|x|}{x} d x+\int_0^b \frac{|x|}{x} d x\begin{aligned} & =\int_a^0 \frac{-x}{x} d x+\int_0^b \frac{x}{x} d x \\ & =\int_a^0(-1) d x+\int_0^b(1) d x \\ & =[-x]_a^0+[x]_0^b \\ & =a+b=b-(-a) \\ & =|b|-|a|\end{aligned}$
Hence, in all cases,
$I=\int_a^b \frac{|x|}{x} d x=|b|-|a|$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $I(m, n)=\int_0^1 t^m(1+t)^n d t$, then the expression for $I(m, n)$ in terms of $I(m+1, n-1)$ is
questions.solution:
Here, $I(m, n)=\int_0^1 t^m(1+t)^n d t$
[We apply integration by parts, taking $(1+t)^n$ as first and $t^m$ as second function]
$\begin{aligned}
& I(m, n)=\left[(1+t)^n \cdot \frac{t^{m+1}}{m+1}\right]_0^1 \\
& \quad-\int_0^1 n(1+t)^{n-1} \cdot \frac{t^{m+1}}{m+1} d t
\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \quad=\frac{2^n}{m+1}-\frac{n}{m+1} \int_0^1(1+t)^{n-1} \cdot t^{m+1} d t \\ & \therefore I(m, n)=\frac{2^n}{m+1}-\frac{n}{m+1} \cdot I(m+1, n-1)\end{aligned}$

questions.solution:
Given that,
$I=\int_0^6 \frac{d x}{1+x^2}$  ....(i)
From Eq. (i), $f(x)=\frac{1}{1+x^2}$
Now, divide the interval $[0,6]$ into six parts each of width
$h=\frac{6-0}{6}=1$
The value of $f(x)$ are given below
$\begin{array}{c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c}\hline x & 0 & 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 & 5 & 6 \\\hline f(x) & 1 & 0.5 & 0.2 & 0.1 & 0.0588 & 0.0385 & 0.027 \\\hline\end{array}
The trapezoidal rule is
$\begin{aligned} \int_{x_0}^{x_0+n h} y d x= & \frac{h}{2}\left[\left(y_0+y_n\right)\right. \\ & \left.+2\left(y_1+y_2+y_3+\ldots+y_{n-1}\right)\right]\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} \therefore \int_0^6 \frac{1}{1+x^2} d x & =\frac{1}{2}[(1+0.027)+2\{0.5+0.2 \\ & +0.1+0.0588+0.0385\}] \\ & =\frac{1}{2}[1.027+2(0.8973)] \\ & =\frac{1}{2}[1.027+1.7946] \\ & =\frac{1}{2}[2.8216]=1.4108\end{aligned}

questions.q:
Let $f(x)$ be a positive function. Let
$\begin{aligned}
I_1 & =\int_{1-k}^k x f\{x(1-x)\} d x, \\
I_2 & =\int_{1-k}^k f\{x(1-x)\} d x,
\end{aligned}$
where $2 k-1\gt0$, then $\frac{I_1}{I_2}$ is
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} I_1 & =\int_{1-k}^k x f\{x(1-x)\} d x \\ & =\int_{1-k}^k(1-x) f\{(1-x)(1-(1-x))\} d x \\ & \quad\left(\because \int_a^b f(x) d x=\int_a^b f(a+b-x) d x\right) \\ & =\int_{1-k}^k(1-x) f\{(1-x) x\} d x \\ & =\int_{1-k}^k f\{x(1-x)\} d x -\int_{1-k}^k x f\{x(1-x)\} d x \\ \Rightarrow & \quad I_1=I_2-I_1 \Rightarrow 2 I_1=I_2\end{aligned}\Rightarrow \quad \frac{I_1}{I_2}=\frac{1}{2}$
